newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols aloft as spot tumbles.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols aloft as spot tumbles.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options whipsawed at sharply higher levels in U.S. trading after soaring earlier on a sudden nosedive in the spot greenback, dealers said.
"It's really choppy," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank. "One-month volatility jumped two percentage points and then came back one point."
Volatilities, which in recent weeks had tended to rise when the dollar tested the upside, shot up overnight as the dollar plunged on remarks by an influential Japanese Finance Ministry official.

Eisuke Sakakibara, the director general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau who played a major role in taming the raging yen last year, said the dollar's recovery from last year's postwar lows was about to finish.

One-month dollar/yen implied volatility jumped about two points from late Wednesday levels to 9.7 percent earlier in the day, then recoiled to about 8.9/9.1 by late U.S. morning. One-year dollar/yen stood at 9.9/10.1 percent, off early highs of 10.2 percent but still more than half a point over Wednesday's levels.
The dollar, which had been hovering in the 113.50-114.50 yen area for most of the week, tumbled below 111.50 yen.
"Dollar/yen always grinds higher but gaps lower," said a trader at a U.S. bank in New York.
He said front-end volatilities would stay very sensitive to the dollar's downside and a fall below 110 yen could confirm an end to the dollar's bull trend.

The market has clearly shifted its focus to the dollar's downside. Risk-reversals, which reflect pricing differentials between puts and calls, jumped to around 1.0 percent in favor of yen calls after being pegged close to par for weeks.
Still, traders cautioned that the dollar had pulled back sharply several times since September last year and yet maintained an upward trend.
Dollar/mark volatilities were more modestly firmer as spot had been contained mostly between 1.5040 and 1.5110 marks.
One-month dollar/mark was quoted at 7.9/8.2 percent, up a quarter point. The volatility curve was very flat, with one-year at 8.2/8.4 percent.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities continued to consolidate as spot cable appeared to be out of steam and stayed well off Monday's $1.6560 high.
Front months, which had risen sharply in the past week, were the hardest hit, with one-month losing nearly half a point from late Wednesday to 8.0/8.3 percent.
Traders expected some more correction in the front end because the volatility curve was still slightly inverted, with six-month at 7.9/8.2 percent.
